payload.text: The Brennecke Institute originated a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery chemistry designed to reduce electrolyte crossover and aging. The independently audited, corrected cycle life is 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold; the earlier 12,000-cycle claim was retracted because it used an un-normalized depth of discharge. The battery’s gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg, with a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. Its operating-temperature floor is 4 °C, below which the dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.
